mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during episodes where GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 8% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when UNRATE exceeds 8% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 3% month-over-month, sustained for two months, reflects supply-side stress that raises input costs and depresses earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO MoM change < -3% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of two consecutive months of >3% MoM INDPRO declines.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 1% month-over-month indicates broad-based demand weakness, which depresses corporate revenues and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline >1% MoM
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) when both GDPC1 and HOUST fall by more than 1% in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is below 1% and CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) rises above 3% for three consecutive months, real interest rates turn negative, boosting present value of cash flows and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1% AND CPIAUCSL > 3% for three consecutive months
regime_hint: ultra-loose monetary policy with inflation surprise
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) during periods when FEDFUNDS < 1% and CPIAUCSL > 3% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid acceleration in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) growth above 250k per month for three consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of three consecutive months with PAYEMS growth above 250,000.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on negative relationship exists between the real savings rate (RSAFS/GDPC1) and S&P 500 forward returns: higher real savings imply more capital available for investment but also lower immediate consumption demand, which historically maps to lower near-term equity valuations over a 5-day horizon.
failure_condition: The correlation between real savings rate (RSAFS/GDPC1) and S&P 500 5-day forward returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05) in out-of-sample walk-forward tests.
